title: Zettafly: A Network Topology with Flexible Non-blocking Regions for Large-scale AI and HPC Systems
problem: Post-exascale and zettascale AI/HPC systems require interconnection networks that support both scalability and non-blocking communication for concurrent jobs, but existing topologies (e.g., fat-tree, dragonfly) lack mechanisms to flexibly partition non-blocking sub-networks to match the small-to-medium job sizes that dominate compute-core-hour consumption in production systems.
motivation: Production supercomputing data shows that small and medium jobs consume the majority of core-hours and generate traffic confined to a subset of the network, yet today's topologies cannot efficiently isolate these jobs into non-blocking regions, causing unnecessary inter-job interference and poor utilization.
method: Zettafly is a two-layer topology family: non-blocking groups (NB groups) at the bottom layer connected by global routers at the top, structured so that any minimally-routed packet between groups traverses at most one global router (low-diameter property). NB groups are sized and configured to match common job sizes, providing non-blocking communication within each group. The paper introduces simple adaptive routing algorithms tailored to Zettafly's structure and evaluates performance, cost, and scalability via extensive simulation against state-of-the-art topologies (fat-tree, dragonfly variants) under HPC workload traffic patterns including multi-task mixed traffic.
key_novelty: A two-layer network topology that decouples non-blocking group size from global scale, enabling flexible partitioning of large networks into non-blocking sub-networks matched to typical HPC/AI job sizes while maintaining low diameter and cost-effectiveness at zettascale.
contributions: Zettafly topology design with non-blocking groups and a single global router hop between groups, supporting flexible partitioning for job isolation.
Adaptive routing algorithms designed for Zettafly's two-layer structure.
Extensive simulation demonstrating cost-effectiveness under multi-task mixed traffic and performance under typical HPC workloads.
Analysis of incremental deployment and flexible configuration for post-exascale and zettascale systems.

metrics.other: Performance and cost improvements vs. fat-tree and dragonfly under multi-task mixed traffic (specific numbers not in abstract)

limitations: Evaluation is simulation-based without physical hardware implementation; specific numbers on speedup or bandwidth improvement are not disclosed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Flexible non-blocking network topology for large-scale AI/HPC interconnects
